Gearbox HS Stage Wear
Rotating equipment
RMS above 2.8 mm/s with rising gear-mesh sidebands.
High-speed pinion tooth wear or bearing fatigue
Agitator stop lets solids settle; restart under load risks shaft damage.
Take an FFT at the input bearing, check oil condition and plan pinion inspection at next stop.
Agitator gearbox may be wearing out
The gearbox driving the tank stirrer vibrates above 2.8 mm/s in a pattern that points to a worn fast gear or bearing. If it stops, solids settle and a restart can damage the shaft.
Check the gearbox oil and vibration at its input bearing, and plan to inspect the small fast gear at the next stop.

R-AGIT-02
Mechanical Seal Overheating
Rotating equipment
Barrier-fluid temperature above 80 °C, rising with constant load.
Loss of barrier-fluid circulation or seal-face distress
Seal leakage of process slurry; vessel must be emptied for seal change.
Check barrier pot level and pressure, thermosiphon flow and cooler; inspect seal faces if trend persists.
Agitator shaft seal is running too hot
The cooling fluid in the seal where the stirrer shaft enters the tank is above 80 °C and climbing. Slurry may start to leak, and the tank would have to be emptied to change the seal.
Check the level, pressure and flow of the seal cooling fluid and its cooler, and inspect the seal if it keeps heating up.

Rotating equipment
Runout above 0.4 mm with 1× running-speed dominance.
Impeller imbalance from build-up or a bent shaft
Seal and gearbox bearing overload; shaft fatigue cracking.
Inspect impeller for build-up or blade loss; check shaft straightness at next stop.
Agitator shaft is wobbling
The stirrer shaft swings more than 0.4 mm off centre each turn, likely from build-up on the blades or a bent shaft. This overloads the seal and gearbox bearings and can crack the shaft.
At the next stop, check the stirrer blades for build-up or missing pieces and check that the shaft is straight.

Girth Gear Mesh Distress
Rotating equipment
Mesh acoustic level above 85 dB with pinion sideband growth.
Insufficient girth-gear lubrication or pinion misalignment
Accelerated tooth pitting; girth gear replacement is a long outage.
Check spray lubrication pattern and quantity; verify pinion alignment by thermography.
Mill's main ring gear may be wearing fast
The large ring gear that turns the ball mill (a drum of steel balls that grinds ore) is loud, above 85 dB. Poor lubrication or misalignment is likely; damaged teeth mean a long shutdown.
Check that the gear spray lubrication reaches the teeth, and have the drive gear alignment checked with a thermal camera.

Mill drive gear bearing may be damaged
The motor-side bearing of the small gear that turns the ball mill vibrates above 3.5 mm/s, typical of a cracked outer ring. If it seizes, the mill stops and the gear can be damaged.
Have the bearing vibration analysed to confirm the damage, and plan a bearing change at the next planned stop.
